name: Alabama
nameStory: Named for the Albaamaha people, whose name most likely came from Choctaw words for 'thicket-clearers' - people who cut back the brush to plant crops. The state is still farm country, so the name describes what people did there 400 years ago and what many still do.
capitalStory: Montgomery bookends American history in about four city blocks. The Confederacy was founded here in February 1861, and Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat here in December 1955 - same downtown, a century apart.

majorFeatures.name: Cheaha Mountain
majorFeatures.note: Southern tail of the Appalachians, 2,413 ft

funFacts: Mobile held America's first Mardi Gras in 1703 - fifteen years before New Orleans existed.
Huntsville is 'Rocket City': the Saturn V that flew to the Moon was designed there.
The 'Black Belt' is named for its dark, rich topsoil, not its people - though that soil is why plantations, and later a Black majority, concentrated there.
The highest point in the state is only 2,413 feet.
whyItMatters: The 1965 Selma-to-Montgomery marches, and the televised police violence at the Edmund Pettus Bridge, pushed Congress to pass the Voting Rights Act within five months.
